votes.refutation: I tried to find a caller that writes output on every streamed event or repeated webhook, making the pre-dedupe fetch a demonstrated load defect. Ordinary state/status PATCHes are excluded by update_fields, and repeated PR webhook writes return without saving. Explicit repeated output writes can indeed produce one additional current-head fetch each, but the claim supplies no reachable high-frequency producer, exhausted quota, or other concrete user-facing failure. The fetch has a tested correctness/recovery purpose and same-head work is already bounded to a fetch plus database checks. A short-lived coalescing key is an optional optimization, not an established defect on this source.

A handled head is a no-op, a stranded QUEUED run is restarted, and failed/changed-head cases can receive a new review; tests/test_tasks.py:974-1001 covers those distinct cases. The hot TaskRun status/state paths are filtered out by products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-89, and the ordinary workflow status writer explicitly omits output at products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/update_task_run_status.py:69. The receiver further restricts dispatch to non-internal signal implementations and opted-in assigned reviewers at receivers.py:98-126. votes.refutation: I first checked whether the alleged many jobs arise from normal frequent TaskRun saves and whether repeated URLs imply redundant work. Status/state-only saves do not publish, and an unchanged URL cannot establish an unchanged head: a later output save is deliberately a backstop for a missed synchronize or failed review. Same-head attempts avoid the expensive sandbox work after one freshness fetch. A short coalescer plus reconciliation could be a reasonable optimization, but the finding provides only potential pressure, not a production workload or correctness/performance failure showing that this bounded recovery check is defective. I therefore reject the issue as speculative load optimization rather than a shipping regression.
